name: blastradius-mcp
description: Zero-trust security proxy for MCP: pre-execution blast radius simulation, DLP redaction, step-up approval tokens, and a hash-chained audit ledger.
long_description: BlastRadius MCP is a local stdio Model Context Protocol server that sits between an AI agent and the tools it wants to call. Before anything executes, `simulate_action` scores the action (danger 0-100), estimates blast radius, and reports how reversible it would be. `inspect_payload_dlp` scans text, code, and logs for API keys, passwords, JWTs, cloud credentials, credit cards, SSNs, and PII, and returns a masked copy. `enforce_policy` is the central decision point: it evaluates a prospective tool call against a policy profile, DLP-scans the parameters, and appends a hash-chained audit entry. High-impact actions require an HMAC-SHA256 signed, time-bound step-up token minted by `request_confirmation_token`, which makes human approval non-repudiable. `verify_audit_log` re-walks the hash chain to detect tampering, deletions, or unauthorized edits, and `get_security_posture` reports live threat statistics, the active policy profile, and DLP redaction totals. The server is fully local: it opens no sockets, sends nothing to third parties, and has no license key or paid tier.

tools.name: simulate_action
tools.description: Simulates and predicts the blast radius, danger score (0-100), and destructive reversibility of a shell command, SQL query, or cloud operation before execution.

commandOrQuery.description: The command, query, or script payload to simulate.

context.description: Execution context such as environment (prod/stage), working directory, or target host.

tools.name: inspect_payload_dlp
tools.description: Deep Data Loss Prevention (DLP) scanner. Detects, reports, and redacts API keys, passwords, JWTs, cloud credentials, credit cards, SSNs, and PII from prompts, code, and logs.

content.description: The raw text, code snippet, or log output to inspect.

maskSensitive.description: Whether to return a sanitized version with credentials and PII masked.

tools.name: enforce_policy
tools.description: The central zero-trust decision point. Evaluates a prospective tool call against organizational security policies, scans parameters for DLP, and records a cryptographic audit trail.

toolName.description: The name of the target tool intended to be called.

parameters.description: The parameters intended to be passed to the tool.

callerId.description: Unique identifier for the calling agent or user.

confirmationToken.description: Optional cryptographically signed approval token for elevated destructive actions.

tools.name: request_confirmation_token
tools.description: Generates a time-bound, cryptographically signed (HMAC-SHA256) step-up approval token allowing an agent to execute high-impact actions when human consent is granted.

toolName.description: The specific tool name to authorize.

actionFingerprint.description: Unique signature or hash of the approved payload.

requestedBy.description: Identifier of the human supervisor or authorizing entity.

tools.name: verify_audit_log
tools.description: Cryptographically verifies the immutable hash-chained audit ledger to detect tampering, deleted records, or unauthorized log modifications.

limit.description: Number of recent audit records to verify.

tools.name: get_security_posture
tools.description: Returns current operational security metrics, the active policy profile, build edition and capabilities, blocked threat statistics, and DLP redaction totals.

signing_key.title: Approval Token Signing Key
signing_key.description: Optional HMAC-SHA256 secret used to sign step-up approval tokens. Leave blank to generate an ephemeral per-process key; approval tokens then stop validating when the server restarts.

audit_key.title: Audit Ledger Hash Key
audit_key.description: Optional HMAC-SHA256 secret used to chain audit ledger entries. Leave blank to generate an ephemeral per-process key; previously written audit entries then fail verification.

policy_file.title: Custom Security Policy File
policy_file.description: Optional path to a JSON security policy config, equivalent to the --policy CLI flag. Leave blank to use the built-in policy profiles.
